The current codebase makes use of the zero-length array language extension
to the C90 standard
column2: but the preferred mechanism to declare variable-length

column1: types such as these ones is a flexible array member[1][2]
struct foo {
int stuff;
struct boo array[];
By making use of the mechanism above
column2: we will get a compiler warning in

column1: case the flexible array does not occur last in the structure
help us prevent some kind of undefined behavior bugs from being
inadvertently introduced[3] to the codebase from now on.
Also
column3: dynamic memory allocations won't be affected by this

column1: change:
Flexible array members have incomplete type
may not be applied. As a quirk of the original implementation of
zero-length arrays
sizeof(flexible-array-member) triggers a warning because flexible array
members have incomplete type[1]. There are some instances of code in which
the sizeof operator is being incorrectly/erroneously applied to zero-length
arrays and the result is zero. Such instances may be hiding some bugs. So
this work (flexible-array member conversions) will also help to get
completely rid of those sorts of issues.
This issue was found with the help of Coccinelle.
[1] https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Zero-Length.html
[2] https://github.com/KSPP/linux/issues/21
